Byte addresses are 6 bits; awaddr[5] = 1 (0x20..0x3F) is out of range, awaddr[1:0] are ignored and the register index is awaddr[4:2]. State: aw_full with aw_addr[5:0]; w_full with w_data[31:0] and w_strb[3:0]; bvalid with bresp[1:0]; all reset to 0. Every output is a view of that state with no combinational path from any input: awready = !aw_full and wready = !w_full (the channels are independent; neither ready waits for the other channel's valid); bvalid and bresp are the registers; with do_write = aw_full && w_full && !bvalid, wr_en = do_write && !aw_addr[5]; wr_idx = aw_addr[4:2], wr_data = w_data and wr_strb = w_strb are shown whatever wr_en is. At each rising edge with rst low, using the state and inputs before the edge: if do_write then aw_full = 0, w_full = 0, bvalid = 1 and bresp = 2 (SLVERR) when aw_addr[5] = 1, else 0 (OKAY); the bank writes at this same edge, so the register update and the response become visible together, and an out-of-range write changes no register. Otherwise, if bvalid && bready then bvalid = 0. Independently, if awvalid && awready then aw_full = 1 and aw_addr = awaddr; if wvalid && wready then w_full = 1, w_data = wdata and w_strb = wstrb. So AW and W may arrive in either order or together, one of each may be held while a response is pending, and a held pair is written only at an edge where bvalid was 0 before the edge (not at the edge where a stalled response retires). A write costs at least two edges, so one write per two cycles is the peak rate. bresp keeps its value after the B transfer. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge returns every register to its reset value; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep the registers in state and return every output as it is after that edge.
